subject: Neighborhood
object: a notion that can be naturally defined using a sliding window over consecutive words
evidence_quote: Given the linear nature of text, the notion of a neighborhood can be naturally deﬁned using a sliding window over consecutive words.

subject: Networks
evidence_quote: Networks, however, are not linear, and thus a richer notion of a neighborhood is needed.

subject: Randomized procedure
object: many different neighborhoods of a given source node
evidence_quote: To resolve this issue, we propose a ran- domized procedure that samples many different neighborhoods of a given source nodeu.

subject: Neighborhoods NS(u)
evidence_quote: The neighborhoods NS(u) are not restricted to just immediate neighbors but can have vastly different structures depending on the sampling strategyS.

subject: Breadth-first Sampling
object: nodes which are immediate neighbors of the source
evidence_quote: The neighborhoodNS is re- stricted to nodes which are immediate neighbors of the source.

subject: Depth-first Sampling
object: nodes sequentially sampled at increasing distances from the source node
evidence_quote: The neighborhood consists of nodes sequentially sampled at increasing distances from the source node.

subject: Homophily hypothesis
object: nodes that are highly interconnected and belong to similar network clusters or communities should be embedded closely together
evidence_quote: Under the homophily hypothesis [7, 36] nodes that are highly interconnected and belong to similar network clusters or communities should be embedded closely together ( e.g., nodes s1 and u in Figure 1 belong to the same network commu- nity).

subject: Structural equivalence hypothesis
object: nodes that have similar structural roles in networks should be embedded closely together
evidence_quote: In contrast, under the structural equivalence hypothesis [10] nodes that have similar structural roles in networks should be em- bedded closely together ( e.g., nodes u and s6 in Figure 1 act as hubs of their corresponding communities).
